level: serious amateur aiming at professional competence

schools.name: Cognitive Load First
schools.optimises_for: retention and transfer for novices working within tight working-memory limits
schools.gives_up: learner autonomy and the motivational payoff of open-ended discovery

schools.name: Constructivist / Discovery
schools.optimises_for: authentic problem-solving, motivation, and ownership through learner-driven inquiry
schools.gives_up: efficiency and protection of novice working memory

schools.name: Backward Design / Assessment-First
schools.optimises_for: tight alignment between the stated goal, the evidence collected, and the activities built
schools.gives_up: responsiveness to needs that emerge mid-course

schools.name: Andragogy / Self-Directed
schools.optimises_for: learner ownership and relevance to the learner's own experience and immediate problems
schools.gives_up: standardization, predictable pacing, and comparability across learners

schools.name: Behaviorist / Mastery Learning
schools.optimises_for: measurable mastery of a defined objective before a learner advances
schools.gives_up: nuance in higher-order transfer and tolerance for learner-chosen paths

clusters.name: Analysis
clusters.gist: figuring out whether training is the right fix, for whom, and what the gap actually is

clusters.name: Objectives
clusters.gist: turning a fuzzy goal into a measurable target and mapping it before you build anything

clusters.name: Design
clusters.gist: choosing and sequencing the instructional strategy that will actually close the gap

clusters.name: Assessment
clusters.gist: proving the objective was met, fairly and validly

clusters.name: Media
clusters.gist: turning the design into built, deliverable material without breaking cognition

clusters.name: Facilitation
clusters.gist: running the live or async session and reading the room

clusters.name: Evaluation
clusters.gist: finding out whether it worked and using that to revise

nodes.label: Training Needs Analysis
nodes.one_line: Tell whether a performance gap is actually a training problem before a budget gets spent building training for it.

nodes.label: Stakeholder & SME Interviewing
nodes.one_line: Pull the real task knowledge out of a sponsor or SME's head instead of the sanitized version they lead with.

nodes.label: Learner Audience Profiling
nodes.one_line: Describe who is actually going to take the course — prior knowledge, motivation, access — well enough to design for them instead of yourself.

nodes.label: Task Analysis
nodes.one_line: Break a job task into the exact steps and decision points an expert makes without noticing.

nodes.label: Gap & Root-Cause Diagnosis
nodes.one_line: Sort a performance gap into its real cause — skill, knowledge, environment, or incentive — instead of defaulting to 'they need training.'

nodes.label: Delivery Context & Constraints Mapping
nodes.one_line: Map the time, budget, technology, and regulatory limits that will rule out design options before you propose them.

nodes.label: SME Collaboration Protocol
nodes.one_line: Run a review cycle with subject-matter experts that gets accurate sign-off without the scope creeping every round.

nodes.label: Bloom's Taxonomy Classification
nodes.one_line: Name the cognitive level a goal actually requires, so 'understand' stops being where every objective quietly lands.

nodes.label: Writing Measurable Learning Objectives
nodes.one_line: Write an objective specific enough that two different people would agree on whether a learner met it.

nodes.label: Prerequisite Mapping
nodes.one_line: Order objectives by what a learner genuinely needs first, not by the order topics appear in the source material.

nodes.label: Backward Design Mapping
nodes.one_line: Decide what counts as evidence of mastery before designing a single activity, so the activities can't drift from the goal.

nodes.label: Objective Review & Critique
nodes.one_line: Catch an objective that's actually an activity, a topic, or an unmeasurable feeling wearing an objective's syntax.

nodes.label: Curriculum Mapping
nodes.one_line: See the whole multi-module curriculum at once well enough to find the gaps and the redundant repeats.

nodes.label: Competency Framework Alignment
nodes.one_line: Map a course's objectives onto an external competency or certification framework without warping either one to fit.

nodes.label: Universal Design for Learning Principles
nodes.one_line: Build one lesson that already works for learners who'd otherwise need three separate accommodated versions.

nodes.label: Instructional Strategy Selection
nodes.one_line: Pick direct instruction, worked examples, PBL, or simulation based on the objective's cognitive demand and the learner's novice/expert level, not habit.

nodes.label: Worked Example Design
nodes.one_line: Show a fully solved problem in a way that reduces a novice's cognitive load instead of just modeling the answer.

nodes.label: Scaffolding & Fading
nodes.one_line: Support a learner just enough to succeed at a task they couldn't do alone yet, then remove the support on a plan, not a whim.

nodes.label: Sequencing & Chunking
nodes.one_line: Break content into pieces sized to working memory and order them so each piece leans on the last.

nodes.label: Active Learning Activity Design
nodes.one_line: Design an activity that makes a learner do the cognitive work the objective actually requires, not just read about it.

nodes.label: Course Blueprint Assembly
nodes.one_line: Produce the single document that specifies every module, activity, and assessment well enough that someone else could build from it.

nodes.label: Formative vs. Summative Assessment
nodes.one_line: Choose whether a check is meant to shape learning in progress or certify it's done, and stop treating a quiz as both.

nodes.label: Writing Selected-Response Items
nodes.one_line: Write a multiple-choice item whose distractors reflect real misconceptions instead of being obviously wrong.

nodes.label: Writing Performance Tasks
nodes.one_line: Design a task that requires demonstrating the skill itself, not recalling facts about it.

nodes.label: Rubric Design
nodes.one_line: Write a rubric with performance levels distinct enough that two raters score the same work the same way.

nodes.label: Assessment Blueprint Construction
nodes.one_line: Produce a test blueprint that maps every item to an objective, so nothing on the assessment is untaught and nothing taught goes unmeasured.

nodes.label: Validity & Reliability Checking
nodes.one_line: Check whether an assessment actually measures the objective it claims to, and whether it does so consistently.

nodes.label: Item Analysis & Revision
nodes.one_line: Read item-level data to find the question that's failing your best learners, and fix or cut it.

nodes.label: Multimedia Learning Principles
nodes.one_line: Apply Mayer's principles (coherence, signaling, redundancy) so added media reduces cognitive load instead of competing for it.

nodes.label: Accessible Media Production
nodes.one_line: Produce media that's usable without sight, hearing, or a mouse, built in from the start instead of retrofitted.

nodes.label: Authoring Tool Fluency
nodes.one_line: Build interactive e-learning content in an authoring tool (Articulate, Rise, H5P) without hand-coding around its limits.

nodes.label: Interactivity Design
nodes.one_line: Design an interaction that requires a real decision from the learner, not a click-to-continue disguised as engagement.

nodes.label: Video & Screencast Production
nodes.one_line: Script, record, and edit instructional video short enough and clear enough that learners actually finish it.

nodes.label: Storyboarding & Build
nodes.one_line: Turn a course blueprint into built, sequenced material — storyboard first, then production — without losing the objective-to-content trace.

nodes.label: Production Review & QA
nodes.one_line: Catch the broken link, mistimed caption, and off-brand asset before a learner does.

nodes.label: Active Listening & Questioning
nodes.one_line: Ask the follow-up question that surfaces what a learner actually thinks instead of what they think you want to hear.

nodes.label: Discussion Design
nodes.one_line: Design a discussion prompt and structure that gets more than the same two people talking.

nodes.label: Feedback Delivery
nodes.one_line: Give feedback specific and timely enough that a learner knows exactly what to do differently next time.

nodes.label: Online Facilitation Technique
nodes.one_line: Run a synchronous or asynchronous online session without the silence, lag, and disengagement that sink most of them.

nodes.label: Difficult Moment Management
nodes.one_line: Handle a derailing question, a dominant participant, or a room that's gone quiet without losing the session's objective.

nodes.label: Facilitation Plan Design
nodes.one_line: Write a facilitator's guide detailed enough that someone other than the designer could run the session and hit the same objectives.

nodes.label: Cohort Facilitation at Scale
nodes.one_line: Facilitate the same course design across multiple cohorts or facilitators while keeping the experience consistent.

nodes.label: Kirkpatrick's Four Levels
nodes.one_line: Place any evaluation question at the right level — reaction, learning, behavior, or results — instead of only ever measuring reaction.

nodes.label: Data Collection Instrument Design
nodes.one_line: Design a survey or observation instrument that measures the outcome you actually care about, not just what's easy to ask.

nodes.label: LMS Analytics Reading
nodes.one_line: Read LMS completion, time-on-task, and drop-off data well enough to tell a real design problem from noise.

nodes.label: Level 3 Transfer Measurement
nodes.one_line: Measure whether a skill actually transferred to the job, not just whether the learner passed the course.

nodes.label: ROI & Business Case Building
nodes.one_line: Build the business case that connects training spend to a measurable organizational outcome a sponsor cares about.

nodes.label: Continuous Improvement Cycle
nodes.one_line: Turn pilot and evaluation data into a scheduled revision instead of a course that ships once and calcifies.

nodes.label: Piloting & Revision
nodes.one_line: Run a course through one real cohort before full launch, and use what breaks to revise it.
